assessment: Strong reusable primitives, explicit character discovery, common non-character drawing contracts, coordinated acting with opt-in transition policies, executable cross-system recipes and scoped numeric regression envelopes. Core callback and prop-option defects have atomic preflight and repairable failures. Common authoring failures now expose explicit repair fields with bounded SDK/CLI payloads. Head mechanics, records, seeded noise, speech analysis and behavioral planning now have separate implementation owners behind the existing public API. Limb transform, gesture, contact and skeletal sampling also have separate owners while retaining public records and shared interpolation. Explicit drawing events now cover synchronous and deferred execution without profiler inference. Rendered caches bind actual renderer and print-font inputs while retaining stable drawing identities. Scoped continuity discovery distinguishes source derivatives, estimated joins and held compiler output. Remaining priorities include broader contracts, bounded scene composition, drawing adoption evidence and broader body/gaze capabilities. Discovery deliberately retains unknown semantics for other non-character families. Numeric validity does not establish perceptual quality.

authoring_benchmark.coverage_scope: The focused pytest-cov invocation exited 1 because its whole-SDK coverage denominator measured 23.02%, below the unchanged 80% gate. The scoped report for all three changed modules passed at 95%; the full repository test suite was not run.
authoring_benchmark.qualification: Real renderer tests verify repeatable phase outputs and decoded plate pixels. Timing is observational, not a correctness threshold. Cold application processes and caches do not flush OS or GPU caches. Hardware/driver identity requires external pinning. The compiler audits the eight emitted frames separately from the nine-point planning grid. A 30-second render limit was too small on this host; correctness integration uses explicit 120-second render and 600-second worker limits. No speedup is claimed.

Legacy flat cache files remain untouched and are not trusted as renderer-owned hits. Returned filenames preserve render identity through copied host assets.

Warm hits still read and hash inputs. Zero new renderer invocations is not a zero-cost lookup guarantee.

findings.title: Preflight location callbacks before drawing any part of the set
findings.problem: office_wide(at_desk=False) silently omits the requested slot; office_wide(at_desk=123) raises raw TypeError after changing the scene. An agent repairing the failed request can retain partial geometry or duplicate a set. _call uses truthiness, and callbacks are reached only after drawing starts.
findings.reproduction: Create a fresh Scene and Canvas(font_asset=None), snapshot scene.to_bytes(), then call locations.office_wide(cv, cv.comp, at_desk=False) or at_desk=123. The former returns successfully; the latter raises TypeError; both change scene.to_bytes().
findings.change: Preflight every core location slot as None or callable before drawing, allocating IDs or registering reusable resources. Report an explicit LocationError code, field path and remedy. Keep callback execution separate from preflight and preserve valid callback ordering.
acceptance: Malformed callbacks fail before scene and canvas state changes
None remains the explicit omitted-slot value
Valid callbacks execute once at their documented drawing depth
A repaired retry has the same output as a fresh successful build
findings.resolution: All 23 core location callback slots are checked as None or callable before drawing resources are created. Falsey callable objects execute rather than disappearing. LocationError exposes location.slot, path, actual, expected and remedy; depth errors now expose the same repair fields and bound extreme numbers. Invalid-slot tests compare scene bytes and canvas state, then prove repaired retries match fresh builds. Existing room/cactus tests retain drawing-depth coverage. This preflight validates callback presence/type; it does not sandbox arbitrary callback bodies or promise rollback of their external effects.

findings.title: Reject malformed prop options instead of silently changing the drawing
findings.problem: chair(style='greay') draws the gray chair, and coffee_cup(shadow='false') draws a contact shadow because the string is truthy. Both return successfully. Generated arguments can therefore produce unintended artwork without a repair signal.
findings.reproduction: On separate fresh canvases, call props.chair(cv, cv.comp, style='greay') and props.coffee_cup(cv, cv.comp, 0, 0, shadow='false'). Both succeed and mutate the scene; neither returns a typed validation failure.
findings.change: Validate the chair style vocabulary and require a boolean shadow option before drawing. Return PropError with path, actual, expected and remedy. Preserve supported placement values and valid output; do not silently coerce strings to booleans.
acceptance: Typos and string booleans fail atomically with actionable fields
Both supported chair styles and both boolean shadow values retain their output
SDK and CLI diagnostic encoding preserve the same repair information
findings.resolution: Chair styles and cup shadow flags are explicitly validated before drawing. Cup placement is validated through detached sr-core group descriptors before allocating IDs, preserving supported relative coordinates and numeric lexical forms. Typed PropError diagnostics include repair fields and remain bounded for extreme integers. Five serialized drawing fingerprints captured before the change still match, including both chair styles and both shadow values. Tests verify custom ID allocators remain untouched by rejected placement and CLI formatting preserves the actual SDK diagnostic fields.

findings.title: Expose explicit transition policies at the coordinated acting boundary
findings.problem: Low-level channels support many curves and springs, and MotionStyle supplies arcs, overshoot and settling. ActingBeat exposes only a transition duration: numeric targets use fixed sampled sine-in-out, while expressions and gestures switch at arrival. Agents cannot select coordinated anticipation, settling or staggered channel timing through the high-level score. Existing action joins match estimated velocities but do not promise acceleration continuity.
findings.change: Add versioned, opt-in transition policies that compile through existing curve and spring mechanics, with explicit channel timing and rig capability checks. Keep held or replacement faces explicit; require authored support for any facial morph. Describe position, velocity and acceleration guarantees separately instead of treating all easing as smoothness.
acceptance: Strict score parsing and discovery describe supported policies
Existing scores retain their current output
Random-access and cut-window parity holds through anticipations and settling
Contact ownership and motion limits survive transitions
Rendered comparisons distinguish intended emotional timing from numeric continuity claims
findings.resolution: Added opt-in versioned TransitionPolicy and ChannelTiming, strict score schema 1.1.0 and capability-dependent discovery. Numeric phases reuse Channel curves and springs with bounded dense baking; held faces, gestures and gaze have separate arrival times. Legacy scores retain their captured serialized drawing, and schema 1.0.0 still rejects new fields. Tests preserve random-access/cut state, contact and prop ownership, reject overlapping phases and reset/contact crossings, enforce head/breath limits even under overrides, and bound adversarial input and work. Engine comparisons cover cuts inside anticipation and settling. The executable three-variant study exports exact scores and source hashes and strictly encodes 96 frames at 1920x1080/24 fps. Four full-size frames demonstrate earlier expression timing and retained state after cuts. Its report explicitly separates authored intent and sampled continuity from perceptual preference, facial morphing and derivative guarantees.

findings.title: Normalize actor placement and timing through explicit adapters
findings.problem: Actor.build, Toon figure wrappers, Gloss drawing functions and plate rigs have different placement and performance contracts. Bento's duration means project exit while its pose starts are relative to enter; limb actions use motion seconds.
findings.change: Introduce a typed adapter boundary with explicit start/end, coordinate units, time conversion and capability checks, preserving existing builders and their defaults.
acceptance: Equivalent performances on nonzero project offsets
No double offset or accidental duration-as-length conversion
Unsupported channels fail before drawing
Existing scenes retain their output without opting in
findings.resolution: Added opt-in typed ActorClip, split-head ToonClip, GlossClip and prepared PlateClip adapters. Interval uses parent start/end seconds; an engine container clock maps local performances once, including idle and limb animation. Placement explicitly maps a source anchor to parent units. Unsupported controls and invalid data are preflighted; failed drawing restores scene/canvas state. Actor's optional end bounds root baking to the clip, preserving the project-duration default. Rafa sheet conversion preserves image patches and source duration. Specialized builders outside these families retain their APIs; shared acting intent and cross-clip state are covered by SDK-P2-02.

findings.title: Add executable cross-system authoring recipes
findings.problem: There are useful runnable examples for individual systems, but agents still need to assemble emotional transitions, state across cuts and multi-rig performances from separate references.
findings.change: Add short executable recipes for sustained listening, a changing emotion, carrying a prop across a cut and the same intent on two rig families. Show valid imports, clocks, capabilities and repairable failures.
acceptance: Documentation examples execute in tests
Examples use public APIs and explicit assets
Output includes machine-readable validation and reproducible render commands
findings.resolution: Added executable sustained-listening and carried-prop state recipes, including capability repair diagnostics and explicit source/shot clocks. The complete acting_continuity study uses public APIs to combine a Bento listener and a depth-composited isolated hand/cup interaction that moves through a camera cut and returns to its support. It ships exact listening-score JSON, serialized motion, a licensed font, source provenance, SDK validation and numeric contact evidence. Synthetic listening inputs are labeled explicitly; the documentation explains measured recording inputs. Together with acting_gallery, the examples cover changing emotion and shared intent on two rig families. The new study strictly encoded all 144 frames at 1920x1080/24 fps without diagnostics. Whole-body carrying and perceptual quality certification remain outside this recipe's claims.

findings.title: Separate head-channel mechanics from speech planning
findings.problem: head_motion.py combines channel interpolation, spring baking, bounds, speech analysis, deterministic noise and behavioral planning. Changes to one concern require reviewing a large shared module.
findings.change: Extract cohesive channel and speech-planning internals while preserving public imports. Keep shared interpolation semantics in one implementation; use the same boundary approach for further motion/contact decomposition when it reduces coupling.
acceptance: Existing imports remain valid
Numeric and serialized output parity at keys, cuts and spring boundaries
No new duplicate sampler or planner behavior
findings.resolution: Extracted five implementation modules behind the existing head_motion facade. All 47 original class/function definitions moved with identical ASTs and no duplicates. Public aliases, signatures, type hints, established internal helper imports and serialized Python record identities are retained. A pre-extraction fixture covers 47 channel cases, composed speaking/listening/facing/noise, cut boundaries, emitted XML and nine protocol-4 record types. Shared curve math and existing bounded caches remain single implementations.

Registered function and class-method instrumentation plus explicit Gloss, News, Inked News and Host ownership replace all profiler, source, closure and frame-local inference in usage tracing. Nine pre-migration builder cases retain exact used parts, figure IDs and scene XML. All eight direct Inked News version combinations are attributed explicitly. Nested and failing drawings preserve scope behavior. Source measurements unwrap functions to retain transitive helper counts.
findings.title: Complete explicit drawing-event instrumentation
findings.problem: Drawing events now identify rig drawings and IDs, but usage tracing still installs a profiler and inspects function source/frames to identify legacy calls and delegates.
findings.change: Move legacy registered builders onto explicit drawing events, then remove inference that is no longer needed. Preserve nested drawing attribution and profiler compatibility during migration.
acceptance: Usage and figure-ID parity across representative builder families
Nested and failing drawings leave observer state clean
Tracing does not depend on availability of Python source or frame-local names

findings.title: Enrich legacy errors with actionable repair fields
findings.problem: The shared diagnostic envelope is available, but many older validation paths only supply a message and class-qualified code. Agents still have to interpret prose when path, expected value or remedy is null.
findings.change: Add explicit stable codes, paths, actual/expected values and remedies to common authoring failures, preserving existing exception types and avoiding inference from message text.
acceptance: SDK and CLI expose the same repair fields
Malformed inputs exercise the failure path
Payloads remain bounded and strict JSON
findings.resolution: Common head style, spring, channel, speech, listening, facing, gaze, placement, actor mouth, blink, visibility and canvas key failures declare codes, input paths, actual/expected values and remedies at their validation source. SDK plugin failures preserve these fields through JSON CLI output. Diagnostic traversal has shared node/text budgets; opaque values and extreme integers do not replace these failures with formatting errors. Blink generation refuses oversized schedules before iteration. A tested repair recipe and task-to-API guide document the agent workflow. Other legacy errors retain null metadata rather than inferred facts.

findings.title: Prove the DRAWING.md composition proposal with animated evidence
findings.problem: The default hybrid drawing method now has a rigid-object implementation in proxy/vehicle and a car_vibe example. DRAWING.md still labels moving-camera and turning-object registration as unproven; forms and paint remain proposed. Its document example verifies structure, not the complete animated contact, receiver, lighting and cost acceptance matrix.
findings.change: Build the documented opt-in adoption spike with moving camera and prop contacts, occlusion, shadow receivers, stable textures, emotional continuity, a cut and warm-cache evidence. Keep unsupported backend capabilities explicit.
acceptance: Pinned SDK/engine/style versions and strict render checks
Temporal stability and registration checks plus full-size visual review
Measured cold/warm plate counts and render cost
Operator approval before style adoption, as required by DRAWING.md

findings.title: Extend constraints to whole-body performance
findings.problem: The reusable spatial solver is centered on arms and hands. Drawn leg poses and Soft's local foot pins and walking cues exist, but there is no shared spatial support/balance or locomotion contract coordinating these across rigs with torso and root motion.
findings.change: Add opt-in torso/root coordination and leg/foot contact primitives with explicit supported anatomy and movement envelopes before expanding to locomotion.
acceptance: Foot contacts retain their world anchors
Support and joint constraints are validated
Random-access deterministic sampling
Rendered weight-shift and step examples

findings.title: Support target-based gaze where rigs can draw it
findings.problem: The shared gaze planner has four named states and held eye transitions. It cannot express continuous target tracking or a richer eye/head relationship across rig families.
findings.change: Introduce typed target gaze with explicit eye/head limits and latency, capability-gated continuous sampling, and deliberate mappings for rigs that only support named states.
acceptance: No silent substitution for unsupported gaze
Target motion remains deterministic across cuts and sampling order
Bounds and eye/head timing tests plus rendered review

findings.title: Benchmark the agent authoring loop before optimizing it
findings.problem: The package eagerly imports registered builders, and existing measurement helpers cover source/build comparisons. There is no single benchmark separating discovery, planning, compilation, rendering and cold/warm cache work.
findings.change: Create representative bounded benchmarks for those phases; optimize only measured bottlenecks while preserving discovery completeness and deterministic output.
acceptance: Separate cold/warm measurements and pinned fixture inputs
Report sample, frame, plate and engine invocation counts
Output-equivalence checks accompany any optimization
No wall-clock performance threshold in ordinary correctness tests
findings.resolution: Added an opt-in, bounded authoring-loop benchmark with fresh-process import/discovery, acting and moving-contact planning, repeated compilation, frame rendering, cold/warm plates and fresh pixel verification. Reports pin fixture parameters, Python sources, package versions and renderer bytes, define per-phase work counts and refuse changed outputs before publication. Scoped plate render sessions expose actual launch attempts, nested budgets and timeouts. No performance optimization or motion-quality improvement is claimed.

agent_authoring_guidance: Discover registered versions, explicit capabilities, coordinate spaces and clocks before choosing a builder; keep unknown metadata unknown.

Use parse_score and compile_performance for supported coordinated intent, character clips for placement, and windows of one performance for cuts. Inspect family capabilities before requesting a channel.

Use opt-in acting policies for coordinated phase and channel timing, and existing MotionStyle, speech-timed actions and head channels for arcs and listening. More noise or more easing does not by itself establish purposeful acting.
Test position, velocity, acceleration, contact and clock continuity as separate properties. Current action joins estimate boundary velocities; they do not promise acceleration continuity.
Validate bounded typed input before emission; repair explicit error paths and avoid retrying into a scene already changed by a failed legacy builder.

Pair scoped numeric checks and strict renders with full-size temporal review and actual blinded ratings for weight, intent and emotional readability. Do not infer perceptual approval from a passing schema or speed limit.
limits: No P0 was confirmed. Earlier callback/option, malformed-input, blink-budget and diagnostic-amplification repairs remain recorded. The refreshed review reproduced additional procedural head-schedule and deferred tracing defects, tracked separately above. This is not an exhaustive claim of defect absence.
Numeric regression tests establish constrained sampled behavior, not continuous collision safety or perceptual preference.
The complete P0-P4 implementation goal remains active; open findings are not represented as completed work.
